Article Title: Nandigram bypoll: Rebel TMC faction says it will back Mamata if she contests

Rebel faction says it may back Mamata in Nandigram

NEW DELHI: A five-member delegation of the rebel Trinamool Congress ( TMC ) faction, led by West Bengal LoP Ritabrata Banerjee, on Saturday met India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM) officials in Delhi over the party’s claim to the TMC symbol.The delegation included Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datta. After the meeting, Banerjee said the talks were “very fruitful” and that the panel had sought documents, which the faction would submit.“We are hopeful because we are the TMC,” Banerjee said, adding that the faction was confident about its claim to the party symbol.On the Nandigram bypoll, Banerjee said the faction had “more or less” decided its candidate but would withdraw it if Mamata Banerjee chose to contest as an independent.Rebel TMC chief whip Akhruzzaman said the faction would take a decision before September 16 and expressed confidence that the TMC symbol would work in its favour. “If she (Mamata Banerjee) stands up from Nandigram to fight the by-elections, we will not field a candidate against her,” she said.Banerjee also claimed that the faction wanted Mamata Banerjee to remain part of the West Bengal Assembly, despite its differences with her. "If, even after the announcement, Mamata Banerjee expresses a desire to fight as an independent, we will withdraw our candidate in our support," he said.Asked whether he was optimistic about securing the TMC symbol, Banerjee replied, “100%.”
Article Summary: Rebel faction says it may back mamata in nandigram bypoll. Five-member delegation of the rebel trinamool congress ( tmc ) faction, led by west bengal lop ritabrata banerjee, met india international institute of democracy and election management.

Article Title: Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary
Article Text:
Yogi Adityanath pays tribute to UP's first CM Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary

Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday paid floral tribute to the state's first chief minister and freedom fighter Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant on his 139th birth anniversary, recalling his contributions to India's freedom struggle, governance and social reforms.Speaking at an event held to mark the birth anniversary, Yogi Adityanath described Pant as a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the revered people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to the memories of Pandit Govind Ballabh Pant ji on the occasion of his auspicious birth anniversary, and offer my humble tributes," Yogi said.Recalling Pant's contribution to the Kakori case, the chief minister said that in 1925, Pant had strongly defended revolutionaries facing a case filed by the British government following the Kakori Train Action.He said Pant actively participated in the freedom movement and resigned as the Premier of Uttar Pradesh after being elected to the post in 1937, choosing instead to join the struggle against British rule."Whether it was the Quit India Movement or other major agitations from time to time for the freedom struggle, he actively took part in them," Yogi said.The Chief Minister highlighted Pant's role after Independence, saying he became the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in 1947, when present-day Uttarakhand was also part of the state."As the first chief minister of Uttar Pradesh... he initiated efforts to present the governance of such a large state as a model of good governance, foster its economic development, and work for the welfare of every section of society," he said.Yogi also recalled Pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.Later, as Union Home minister from 1954, Pant worked to address linguistic conflicts and played an important role in establishing Hindi as the official language, Yogi said."On this occasion, on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh and the people of Uttar Pradesh, I pay homage to his memory and offer my humble tributes to him," the chief minister said.
Article Summary: Yogi adityanath pays tribute to up's first cm govind ballabh pant on his 139th birth anniversary. Yogi: pant was a great advocate and freedom fighter who played a significant role in the country's struggle for independence. He recalled pant's contribution to land reforms and described the model introduced during his tenure as exemplary.

Article Title: Elephant Madhuri now on her way to Kolhapur as Anant Ambani's Vantara vows continued medical care
Article Text: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as Mahadevi in Kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city after the High-Powered Committee (HPC) passed an order on September 9, Anant Ambani’s Vantara said in a statement on Thursday.According to Vantara, the HPC permitted Madhuri’s return after hearing the parties' claims, reviewing reports, and inspecting the facility at Nandani in Maharashtra. The order has laid down several conditions, including that Madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.The elephant will also need round-the-clock care and a medical examination every fortnight, Vantara said.Madhuri was brought to Vantara in Jamnagar on July 30, 2025, in compliance with directions from the HPC, which the Bombay High Court and the Supreme Court upheld. Vantara said it had not sought her custody but had received and cared for her in accordance with the directions.The organisation said Madhuri’s health had stabilised after sustained veterinary care, but her chronic conditions still require supportive management and regular monitoring.As part of the transition, Vantara said it had helped arrange living conditions, veterinary infrastructure, medical equipment, medicines and other necessities at the Nandani facility. Its veterinarians will visit Madhuri in Kolhapur every fortnight to conduct her medical examination and submit reports to the competent authorities, as directed by the HPC.Vantara also said it had worked to improve the enclosure at Nandani within the available infrastructure. Further upgrades, it said, were currently restricted by town-planning constraints, including a road passing through land belonging to the trust.The organisation added that it would remain available to support future upgrades at the facility and would assist if directed by the courts or competent authorities.“Madhuri’s wellbeing remains Vantara’s first concern. Our commitment to her health, welfare and dignity does not depend on where she lives,” the statement said.
Article Summary: Madhuri, the elephant popularly known as mahadevi in kolhapur, will be allowed to return to the city. The high-powered committee (hpc) passed an order on september 9, anant ambani’s vantara said. The order has laid down several conditions, including that madhuri cannot be used in processions or for any other purpose.

Article Title: India to get another major DRDO missile testing range in Bengal
Article Text:
The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a boost for the country's defence testing capabilities, India will get another weapon and missile testing range in Bengal's Junput coastal village in Purba Medinipur district.In April 2024, DRDO had proposed a testing range along the Purba Medinipur coast to complement its integrated testing range in Odisha's Chandipur. However, the then TMC govt had not given land for it. During an event Friday, CM Suvendu Adhikari revealed that DRDO had sent a letter for the project but the then TMC govt at the helm did not respond. "I have okayed it. This will be a big project for West Bengal's development," he said. A source in DRDO also confirmed to TOI that the missile testing project is coming up in Bengal.The proposed testing range in Junput will be the third major hub for DRDO after the Chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in Andhra. India has one missile testing facility, known as the Integrated Test Range, which operates across two launch complexes in Odisha: Launch Complex-III at Chandipur-on-Sea and Launch Complex-IV, off Odisha coast.While Launch Complex-III is used primarily for testing short-range tactical missiles, surface-to-air systems and multi-barrel rocket launchers like the Akash and Pinaka, Launch Complex-IV is designated for long-range strategic weapon trials, including Agni ballistic missile series and K-series submarine-launched missiles.The Chandipur testing facility provides a secure coastal location with a wide, unobstructed eastward trajectory over the Bay of Bengal. The proposed Junput range, located approximately 70km along the Bay of Bengal from Chandipur, will share the workload of the Odisha testing range.
Article Summary: The proposed testing range in junput will be the third major hub for drdo after the chandipur sites and the proposed testing centre in andhra. India has one missile testing facility, known as the integrated test range, which operates across two launch complexes in odisha.

Article Title: Delhi 2047: The big plan, the bigger question
Article Text:
Build denser, live better? Delhi’s high-rise gamble under MPD-2047

A locality in delhi, the building density. Photo credit: ANI

More homes, but still affordable?

Demand could hit 1,600 MGD by 2047

So, can MPD-2047 be sustainable?

Can the city’s infrastructure keep pace?

By 2047, Delhi could be home to nearly 32 million people, need around 1,600 million gallons of potable water every day, generate nearly 26,000 tonnes of solid waste daily and require roughly 40 lakh additional homes.Those numbers tell a bigger story than population growth. They point to a city that will need to build more — while somehow using less land, less water and fewer resources, without compromising safety, mobility, liveability or the environment.That is the challenge at the heart of the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 (MPD-2047).The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) unveiled the MPD-2047 at the National Media Centre on August 20, 2026, presenting it as the fourth master plan for the capital, with a perspective extending to 2047. The authority has described the plan as a framework for shaping Delhi’s future growth, with its focus spanning housing, mobility, infrastructure, environmental sustainability and efficient land use.The plan comes after earlier master plans for 1962, 2001 and 2021. DDA’s current master-plan framework includes policies on transit-oriented development, land pooling, redevelopment of ageing neighbourhoods and ecological restoration, placing long-term urban growth alongside infrastructure capacity and sustainability.It envisions a denser, more connected and more transit-oriented Delhi, with large-scale housing, redevelopment of ageing neighbourhoods, stronger public transport, green-blue networks, ecological restoration and new approaches to land and infrastructure planning. It also pushes for compact growth, with development increasingly tied to the capacity of roads, public transport, water, drainage, sewerage and other essential services.But there is a larger question: Can Delhi grow at this scale without repeating the problems that already make the city struggle today?The question becomes harder to ignore when incidents such as the recent Satya Niketan building collapse enter the conversation. The tragedy exposed something the master plan itself acknowledges: planning a city is not enough if building safety, approvals, enforcement and infrastructure do not keep pace with growth.So, what does MPD-2047 promise, and can Delhi actually deliver it?Housing is perhaps the plan’s biggest promise. MPD-2047 estimates the city’s housing requirement at nearly 40 lakh dwelling units by 2047. The strategy combines affordable housing, rental housing, EWS housing, hostels and dormitories, affordable rental housing complexes and redevelopment of existing areas. The government says around 18 lakh affordable homes could come through transit-oriented development, while redevelopment of existing group and government housing could add around seven lakh dwelling units.Land pooling is another major pillar, with the DDA hoping to unlock large areas of land and potentially facilitate up to 20 lakh homes.This is sensible in a land-constrained city. But “affordable” is not simply a number of units. A home is affordable only if households can afford its purchase or rent, utilities, maintenance and commute.That makes displacement an important question. Redevelopment and densification can raise land values and change neighbourhood economics. The success of the housing strategy will therefore depend not only on how many homes are built, but who can actually continue to live in them.MPD-2047 also brings Delhi’s 357 villages into the larger redevelopment conversation. At a conference organised by the Dilli Dehat Project, speakers argued that the plan treats these villages primarily as areas for “regeneration”, rather than recognising them as historic settlements with distinct social, cultural and ecological assets. They also raised concerns about the protection of village commons such as ponds and grazing land, and the impact of road widening and land pooling on existing communities.MPD-2047 moves Delhi towards more compact development. It promotes redevelopment of brownfield areas, mixed-use development and transit-oriented growth, while encouraging higher intensity around mass-transit corridors. The plan also allows buildings of more than 100 floors to be developed as landmark projects in areas with adequate infrastructure.The idea is to support compact growth, reduce urban sprawl and free up more ground-level space for public and green areas. But density is not automatically sustainable.Concentrating growth near Metro and other mass-transit corridors can also make public transport more viable. Sustainability of vertical growth will depend on what surrounds these towers — transport, water, sewage, power, fire safety and open space. Building higher can save land, but only if infrastructure rises with it.Every additional floor brings additional demand for water, sewage, electricity, roads, parking, fire services, schools, healthcare and drainage. MPD-2047 itself takes an infrastructure-led approach: new development is intended to be supported by roads, public transport, water, sewerage, drainage, power and digital connectivity.The real test, therefore, is sequencing.Can infrastructure capacity be demonstrated before density is increased?That may be one of the most important implementation questions for MPD-2047.Water may be the plan’s clearest sustainability test.In 2021, Delhi’s water supply was about 935 MGD, against estimated demand of around 1,380 MGD. By 2047, potable-water demand is projected at approximately 1,600 MGD. The detailed augmentation calculation identifies about 401 MGD of additional supply, taking projected availability from roughly 1,000 MGD to about 1,401 MGD.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.That leaves an apparent gap of roughly 200 MGD against the 1,600 MGD demand estimate.The figures come from different stages and assumptions within the planning calculations, so they should not be treated as a simple supply-versus-demand failure. But they do highlight a genuine vulnerability: Delhi’s future growth cannot depend on finding water after development has already happened.Water recycling, rainwater harvesting, wastewater treatment, groundwater recharge and demand management therefore need to move from supporting provisions to core infrastructure.As MoHUA secretary D Thara recently told real-estate developers, housing projects need green areas, rainwater harvesting, water recycling and sewage-treatment infrastructure rather than simply buildings and roads.The Satya Niketan building collapse has put Delhi’s student housing and building-safety systems under scrutiny. A five-storey boys’ paying guest accommodation near Delhi University’s South Campus collapsed in September 2026, killing seven people, including five university students.The wider question is how safely Delhi’s high-density neighbourhoods are being managed. In Rajendra Nagar, severe waterlogging and drainage failures have repeatedly disrupted life, while the deaths of civil-services aspirants in a flooded coaching-centre basement in 2024 exposed serious gaps in building use, drainage and enforcement. Similar concerns have emerged around cramped PGs, narrow lanes and ageing buildings in student hubs.These incidents underline that urban growth is not only about adding housing and infrastructure. As MPD-2047 enables redevelopment and greater density, building permissions, structural safety, drainage, inspections and emergency access will have to keep pace.The real question is not how high Delhi can build, but how safely it can grow.Yes — the plan has the ingredients for a more sustainable Delhi: compact growth, transit-oriented development, affordable housing, green-blue infrastructure and infrastructure-led planning.But a plan is only a framework. Its success will depend on coordinated implementation, enforcement and infrastructure capacity.The key question is simple: Can Delhi build capacity as fast as it builds density?If yes, MPD-2047 could make Delhi more connected, resilient and resource-efficient. If not, it could simply make today’s problems bigger.The plan sets the direction. Delivery will determine the outcome.
Article Summary: The delhi development authority (dda) unveiled the mpd-2047 on august 20, 2026, presenting it as the fourth master plan for the capital. It envisions a denser, more connected and more transit-oriented delhi, with large-scale housing, redevelopment of ageing neighbourhoods, stronger public transport, green-blue networks and ecological restoration.

Article Title: Rajnath: Modi blunted oppn's 'false narrative' with governance
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh

New Delhi: PM Modi has blended good governance with participatory democracy to render the opposition's "false narrative" and anti-incumbency factor irrelevant, defence minister Rajnath Singh said Saturday, virtually kick-starting BJP's campaign to mark its pre-eminent leader's 25-year unbroken run as head of govt."Those building false narrative against Modi cannot understand what they should do. Sometimes they incite students, sometimes they try to divide society in the name of caste," he said in an apparent swipe at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi.He said that when people see their lives changed by welfare schemes for farmers, housing and health, then no narrative works. "Kaam bolta hai (work speaks). Modi has left factors like astroturfing and anti-incumbency behind," he said at the event organised by Rambhau Mhalgi Prabodhini, a research and leadership-training institute with links to BJP.Rajnath said Modi, since his days as Gujarat CM, pioneered a model of governance that focused on a participatory model of democracy and scaled it nationally as PM.
Article Summary: Defence minister rajnath singh: those building false narrative against modi cannot understand what they should do. "kaam bolta hai (work speaks) modi has left factors like astroturfing and anti-incumbency behind," he said.

Article Title: Grouping eyes mechanism for extradition of eco fugitives
Article Text:
Brics Summit 2026

New Delhi: In a unified resolve to combat money laundering and corruption, Brics nations Saturday reiterated their commitment to "effectively identify, detect and disrupt money laundering schemes" and strengthen digital financial security, including prevention of fraud in cross-border payment systems. For the first time, the grouping emphasised putting in place a mechanism to extradite fugitives from each other's country and initiate steps for asset recovery from such criminals."We welcome the establishment of Brics Expert Network on Asset Recovery to enhance cooperation among focal points and the Brics repository on informal cooperation for tracing fugitive offenders sought for corruption and supporting extradition," the joint declaration stated. There is an ongoing discussion on developing a network of law enforcement agencies for enhancing cooperation on actions against fugitive offenders.The member nations also pledged to "promote cooperation in prevention and combating of corruption and to the continued implementation of relevant international agreements, in particular UN Convention against Corruption."The declaration expressed concern over illicit financial flows, including the financing of terrorism, trafficking of firearms and people, laundering of drug-related crime proceeds and use of communication technologies for criminal purposes.The use of cryptocurrencies and other virtual assets by such networks have an adverse impact on economic stability, sustainable development and the integrity of the international financial system, it said.Without naming the Golden Triangle countries (Myanmar, Thailand and Laos) the group expressed "serious concern over proliferation of organised scam networks, including cross-border fraud operations and so-called scam compounds, which exploit digital technologies, payment systems and individuals in vulnerable situations". TNN
Article Summary: For the first time, the grouping emphasised putting in place a mechanism to extradite fugitives from each other's country. There is an ongoing discussion on developing a network of law enforcement agencies for enhancing cooperation on actions against fugitive offenders.

Article Title: Group embraces AI but silent on those who may lose their jobs
Article Text:
Leaders at Brics Summit

NEW DELHI: Brics has set out an ambitious plan to prepare people for an AI-driven economy, but its New Delhi Declaration leaves a key question largely unanswered - what happens to workers whose jobs are lost or sharply changed because of automation and AI?It calls AI an "immense opportunity to stimulate economic growth and sustainable development for all", while stressing safety, security, inclusion and reliability. But on employment, its response is largely to prepare workers for changing skill needs rather than spell out what happens when technology replaces existing work, reports Manash Gohain. It commits Brics nations to strengthen cooperation in "forecasting skills needs by analysing labour market trends in digital, green, care and other priority sectors".
Article Summary: Leaders at brics summit set out ambitious plan to prepare people for an ai-driven economy. New delhi declaration leaves a key question largely unanswered - what happens to workers whose jobs are lost or sharply changed because of automation and ai? It calls ai an "immense opportunity to stimulate economic growth and sustainable development for all"

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Saturday met with the representatives of both factions of Trinamool Congress , one headed by former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and the other group headed by West Bengal leader of opposition Ritabrata Banerjee, amid their competing claims to being the real party entitled to the use of its "twin flower" poll symbol.The meeting with EC, amid the dispute over the party's authorised signatories and organisational elections, gains significance as it comes ahead of the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly bypolls scheduled for Oct 6. Given that the nominations must be filed by Sept 16, EC may need to take an interim call before that on which of the two factions may contest on the TMC's reserved symbol, in case both wish to field their own candidates.While the faction led by Mamata claimed there was no internal dispute in the party as the rebel faction was "just a bunch of traitors" and that the national working committee was very much within its five-year term, the Ritabrata faction argued that the party constitution provided for a three-year term that had ended in Feb 2025.Mamata's faction deputed a five-member delegation, comprising Derek O'Brien, Kalyan Banerjee, Sagarika Ghose, Saket Gokhale and advocate Abhinav Singh, to present its arguments."There is the Mamata Banerjee-led party on one side and a bunch of traitors on the other. These MLAs received Rs 25 lakh in their bank accounts from the party to contest elections," it said in a statement.Besides Ritabrata, the five-member delegation of the rebel faction included Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datt.

JAMMU: Decomposed remains of a suspected Pakistani Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) terrorist was found Saturday along with an M4 rifle in Divshetar area of J&K’s Doda district, with security forces suggesting the corpse had been lying in the snow-capped hills since the man’s death in a past operation.Some locals noticed the body in Seoj Dhar zone and intimated authorities. “Security forces are conducting further investigations to ascertain the identity of the deceased and other details,” an official said.A J&K Police post on X, apparently aimed at terrorists, pointed towards an encounter death. “You Can Run But You Can’t Hide. Article Title: Brics resolve for joint mechanism to extradite fugitives
Article Text:
The declaration expressed concern about illicit financial flows, including financing of terrorism & more

NEW DELHI: In a unified resolve to combat money laundering and corruption, the Brics member nations on Saturday reiterated their commitment to “effectively identify, detect and disrupt money laundering schemes” and strengthen digital financial security, including prevention of fraud in cross-border payment systems.The grouping for the first time emphasised on putting a mechanism to extradite fugitives from each other’s country and initiate steps towards asset recovery from such criminals.“We welcome the establishment of Brics Expert Network on Asset Recovery to enhance cooperation among focal points and the BRICS repository on informal cooperation for tracing fugitive offenders sought for corruption and supporting extradition,” the joint declaration stated. There is an ongoing discussion on developing a network of law enforcement agencies for enhancing cooperation on actions against fugitive offenders.The member nations also pledged to “promote cooperation in the prevention and combating of corruption and to the continued implementation of relevant international agreements, in particular the UN Convention against Corruption.”The declaration expressed concern about illicit financial flows, including financing of terrorism, trafficking of firearms and people, laundering of drug related crimes proceeds and use of communication technologies for criminal purposes.The use of crypto currencies and other virtual assets by such networks through organized crimes have an adverse impact on economic stability, sustainable development and the integrity of the international financial system, it said.Without naming the Golden Triangle countries Myanmar, Thailand and Laos, the group expressed “serious concern over proliferation of organized scam networks, including cross-border fraud operations and so-called scam compounds, which exploit digital technologies, payment systems and individuals in vulnerable situations”.Members felt the need for a coordinated action to dismantle these illegal networks, trace and recover criminal proceeds, protect victims, and prevent the misuse of financial institutions.

Article Title: Amid AAP-GFP alliance buzz ahead of Kejriwal's visit, Goa Cong says talks on with Sardesai's outfit
Article Text:
Hoardings featuring the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Goa Forward Party (GFP) along Goa’s highways.

Panaji, Hoardings featuring the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Goa Forward Party (GFP) surfaced along Goa's highways on Saturday, sparking buzz of a new front emerging in the coastal state ahead of AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal's visit.However, the Congress said alliance talks with the Vijai Sardesai-led GFP were underway for the 2027 assembly polls.Displaying the slogan, "Don't let them cheat you the third time", the hoardings with symbols of AAP and GFP signal an imminent pre-poll arrangement between Kejriwal's party and the Vijai Sardesai's outfit for the 2027 state elections."Am going to Goa today to make a very big announcement," Kejriwal wrote on his X handle on Saturday morning, even as AAP functionaries confirmed he would arrive in the state later during the day.The GFP is a regional outfit led by former deputy chief minister Sardesai, who is the party's lone MLA in the state assembly, while the AAP has two MLAs - Venzy Viegas and Cruz Silva - representing Benaulim and Velim constituencies respectively in South Goa.A senior GFP functionary said Kejriwal will address a press conference on Sunday during which the alliance between the AAP and GFP would be announced.It would be a non-BJP and non-Congress alliance, he said.The state executive of the Goa Forward Party met on Saturday and resolved to immediately move towards an alliance with like-minded secular political forces to unitedly defeat the BJP in the February 2027 Goa Assembly elections.In a social media post, GFP has said "Our message is clear: Goa First. Before party, before politics and before personal ambitions -- Goa First"."This Chovoth (Ganesh Chaturthi), we will strive to give the people of Goa a United Alternative, one that puts Goa first, protects Goemkarponn, and stands firmly against corruption, communalism and the politics of defection," the GFP said.Meanwhile, Goa Congress president Girish Chodankar told reporters here that the GFP has been an ally since 2022 and was still in talks with his party."The Goa Forward Party is in talks with Congress' central leadership for the 2027 Goa Assembly election pre-poll alliance. I have confirmed with my high command even today morning. They have said that the talks for alliance are still on," Chodankar said.The GFP fought the 2022 assembly election in alliance with the Congress, while the AAP had contested on its own. The Sardesai-led party was in talks with the Congress for a pre-poll alliance for the 2027 state elections but had later stalled the discussion, citing no response from the latter.The elections for the Goa legislative assembly are due before March 2027. Article Title: First Akash, then Ishan, now Deepika: A new twist in Mayawati's succession story takes another turn
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Saturday ruled out any political position for her brother Anand Kumar's sons, Akash Anand and Ishan Anand, calling it her “final decision”, while allowing for the possibility of her niece Kumari Deepika Anand assisting her father with party responsibilities.The announcement came days after Mayawati “freed” her nephew Akash Anand from the party, adding a fresh turn to the BSP's leadership and succession debate ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.In a lengthy post on X in Hindi, Mayawati said she remained focused on the interests of the “Bahujan Samaj family” and reiterated her opposition to political nepotism.“Like Kanshi Ram ji, I too have always kept my brothers, sisters, young family members, and close relations away from positions as MP, MLA, minister, or any other post offering political benefit, by confining them to party work,” she said.Mayawati said Anand Kumar had remained with her and had been handling important party responsibilities under her supervision.“Not only this, since I am unmarried, I am forced to keep one of my siblings -- finally my youngest brother Anand Kumar -- with me. He not only takes care of me but has also been carrying out important party responsibilities under my supervision for a long time. However, if his family members also take advantage of this, then it will not be in the interest of the party and the movement,” she said.Making her decision explicit, Mayawati said, “Therefore, today it is my final decision and pledge that in return, none of his sons, in particular, will be allowed to engage in politics by holding any position, big or small, within the BSP.”She said Anand Kumar could instead seek assistance from his daughter, who is currently studying law.“If Anand Kumar, while remaining with me, needs another member to assist him, then in the current political situation, he can seek the help of his only daughter, Kumari Deepika Anand,” Mayawati said.She added that if Deepika Anand was unwilling, her father could, with the party's consensus, hand over his responsibilities to another “missionary worker” from the party's Dalit community.“This is the need of the hour and in the party's best interest,” she said.Mayawati also invoked Kanshi Ram's opposition to nepotism, saying she remained committed to the principle as his disciple.Meanwhile, she announced a parallel push for younger leadership, saying the BSP was working to ensure around 50 per cent participation of Gen-Z in its organisation. She said the party was also prioritising “dedicated and young talents from all sections of society” as candidates for the Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab Assembly elections due in 2027.The BSP chief said the aim was “so that the constitutional values can rapidly flourish in the country through the new generation”.
Article Summary: Bahujan samaj party chief mayawati rules out any political position for her brother anand kumar's sons, akash anand and ishan anand. She allows for the possibility of her niece kumari deepika anand assisting her father with party responsibilities.

NEW DELHI: Brics leaders on Saturday asserted that they recognised women as leaders, decision-makers and key drivers of economic growth and social transformation.In a joint declaration issued after their meeting, the leaders also acknowledged the vital role of women in peacebuilding in line with the global Women, Peace and Security agenda."We affirm that women's participation in governance; Article Title: Air India pilot dies during Delhi layover
Article Text:
Air India

NEW DELHI: A Mumbai-based Air India pilot died during a Delhi layover on Friday. The pilot, in his 40s, had recently moved from Air India Express to AI. He was found unconscious at his room in The Gran, Vasant Kunj, and rushed to a hospital where he was declared dead.“Air India is deeply saddened at the passing away of a cockpit crew member in Delhi last night. He was on a layover rest at a hotel in Delhi where he was found unconscious last evening. He was rushed to the hospital immediately, where he was declared dead. Air India is in close touch with his family and is extending all support at this time of grief,” an AI spokesperson said.Delhi Police said the pilot had checked into the hotel on Thursday. On Friday evening his brother contacted the hotel manager, saying he was not responding to calls. “The hotel manager went to the pilot’s room and found it locked from inside. The room was opened with the help of hotel master key. (He) was found lying unconscious and unresponsive,” said the police.“The deceased’s post-mortem examination was conducted at Safdarjung Hospital on Saturday. The final cause of death shall be ascertained after receipt of the final opinion. Further enquiry is in progress,” the police added.
Article Summary: Mumbai-based air india pilot died during a delhi layover on friday. The pilot, in his 40s, had recently moved from air india express to ai. He was found unconscious at his room in the gran, vasant kunj, and rushed to hospital.

Article Title: Moldova extradites wanted Punjab gangster Amritpal Singh to India after Red Notice
Article Text:
Amritpal Singh extradited from Moldova to face multiple criminal cases in Punjab

Arrest in Moldova after Interpol Red Notice

Wanted in multiple Punjab cases

NEW DELHI: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), in coordination with the ministry of external affairs (MEA), ministry of home affairs (MHA) and Punjab Police, has secured the extradition of Red Notice subject Amritpal Singh alias Gurpal Singh from Moldova to India, the agency said.Singh is wanted in multiple serious criminal cases in Punjab, including double murder using firearms and offences under the Arms Act and NDPS Act. His criminal antecedents also include cases related to forgery, cheating, use of forged documents and violations of the Passport Act, according to the CBI.The extradition followed a request from Punjab Police, after which the CBI secured an Interpol Red Notice against Singh. He was subsequently located and arrested by Moldovan authorities.Following due legal process, Moldova granted his extradition to India, the CBI said.A four-member Punjab Police team travelled to Chisinau, Moldova, to bring Singh back to India. The team, along with Singh, arrived in Delhi on September 12.Singh, also known as Amrit Dalam, was among the most wanted gangsters linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria gang.The report said he was detained near the Moldova border based on an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Punjab Police in coordination with the MEA, CBI and other central agencies.He’s a native of Dalam Nangal village in Batala and had fled India using a fake passport and was allegedly making extortion calls to businessmen, particularly in the Amritsar region.Punjab Police had also established the Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC), headed by IG-Counterintelligence Ashish Choudhary, to track criminals hiding abroad and pursue their extradition to Punjab.Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav had said Singh was wanted in several serious cases, including murder, attempted murder and drug smuggling.He had also said Singh's detention followed international coordination and follow-up by Punjab Police agencies, while legal and diplomatic procedures were being pursued for his extradition or deportation to India.The latest extradition brings Singh back to India to face the criminal cases registered against him in Punjab.
Article Summary: Amritpal singh, also known as amrit dalam, was among the most wanted gangsters linked to the jaggu bhagwanpuria gang. He was detained near the moldova border based on an interpol red notice issued at the request of punjab police in coordination with the mea, cbi and other central agencies.

Article Title: NIA raids 10 locations across Jammu & Kashmir in LeT-linked terror conspiracy case
Article Text:
NIA searches J&K locations to trace LeT handlers’ local support network (file photo)

Investigation began with OGW arrest

NIA examines financial, communication trails

Hafiz Saeed warrant in related terror case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Saturday conducted searches at 10 locations across Jammu and Kashmir in connection with a cross-border terror conspiracy involving Pakistan-based handlers of the proscribed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) and their alleged network of local Over Ground Workers (OGWs).The searches were carried out in Kupwara, Kulgam, Bandipora, Baramulla and Sopore to gather further evidence related to the conspiracy and ascertain the roles of individuals allegedly providing logistical and other support to infiltrated terrorists, the NIA said.During the searches, incriminating material relevant to the case was seized or secured, according to the agency. The material is being examined and corroborated with other evidence collected during the investigation.The case was initially registered at Police Station Zakoora in Srinagar and was subsequently re-registered by the NIA under Section 23 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, Sections 7 and 25 of the Arms Act, 1959, and Section 4 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.The investigation began after the arrest of an alleged LeT-linked OGW at a naka point during the night of March 31, 2026. A hand grenade and live ammunition were recovered from his possession, the NIA said.Further investigation led to the arrest of Pakistani nationals allegedly linked to the conspiracy and helped investigators identify the suspected roles of members of the local support network.According to the NIA, the investigation so far has revealed links between Pakistan-based LeT handlers and their local associates. These associates were allegedly being used for communication, movement and concealment of infiltrated terrorists, as well as providing shelter, conducting reconnaissance and facilitating other logistical requirements.The agency is also examining the financial trail, communication channels and movement of the accused, along with the source and supply chain of arms and explosives.The objective, according to the NIA, is to establish the complete network and determine the extent of its activities.The latest searches are part of the agency's continuing investigation into the larger conspiracy and the support mechanism allegedly facilitating cross-border terrorism.The NIA said it would continue its investigation to identify all persons involved in the alleged conspiracy and establish their respective roles. Further legal action, including arrests and recoveries, may follow depending on the outcome of the investigation.The searches come amid the NIA's wider investigations into LeT-linked terror networks in Jammu and Kashmir.A Special Court in Jammu on September 8 issued a non-bailable warrant against LeT founder Hafiz Saeed in a terror case related to the alleged supply of weapons, funds and directions to terror groups operating in the Union Territory.It was the second non-bailable warrant issued against Saeed by the Special NIA Court in Jammu in two months.The warrant was issued after the NIA described Saeed, a resident of Sargodha in Pakistan's Punjab province, as an “absconding accused” in a case concerning the arrest of Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat during a check at Pandach on the outskirts of Srinagar earlier this year.A China-made grenade and 15 live rounds were recovered from Bhat, who was booked under the UAPA, Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act.The subsequent investigation led to the alleged busting of a terror network and the arrest of several more terrorists associated with LeT and its offshoot The Resistance Front (TRF), as well as two Pakistani nationals.The NIA told the court that Saeed was allegedly operating from Pakistan and providing weapons, money and directions to terrorists in the Kashmir Valley.The court observed that Saeed's involvement had surfaced during the investigation and that he was “allegedly involved in terrorism”.The latest warrant followed an earlier non-bailable warrant issued against him on July 8 in connection with the Pahalgam terror attack case.
Article Summary: Nia searches j&k locations to trace let handlers’ local support network.investigation began with ogw arrest.nia examines financial, communication trails.hafiz saeed warrant in related terror case issued against him.

Article Title: Why Vijay's gold ring scheme may miss its September 15 launch
Article Text:
Under Vijay's gold ring scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.

What is the gold ring scheme?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's gold ring scheme, which was scheduled to be launched on September 15, shall be deferred from its expected date. The announcement comes as the CM prepares for his first official overseas visit to London. Vijay is set to meet European industrialists during the visit and pitch Tamil Nadu as an investment destination.Vijay will leave Chennai for London via Dubai on Wednesday night and is expected to stay in the UK capital for a few days. He will travel on an Emirates Airlines passenger flight.During the visit, Vijay is expected to invite European companies to set up businesses in Tamil Nadu and seek fresh investment commitments for the state. Senior officials from the industries and finance departments are also expected to travel to London. Some may leave ahead of the chief minister to prepare for his meetings with prospective investors.The visit comes soon after the ‘Vettri Tamil Nadu Investment Conclave 2026’, where the state government announced investment commitments worth Rs 1,02,514 crore through 104 memorandums of understanding (MoUs).Security and protocol arrangements for Vijay’s departure are also being finalised.A high-level Advance Security Liaison meeting is reportedly scheduled at Chennai’s old airport on Wednesday to review the arrangements.Vijay’s London visit also comes amid key political developments in Tamil Nadu. Before leaving for the UK, he is scheduled to chair a second alliance coordination meeting at the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam headquarters in Panaiyur.The meeting is expected to discuss the structure of the ruling alliance and post-poll coalition arrangements. A Common Minimum Programme is also on the agenda, along with discussions on a steering committee and an official name for the alliance.Invitations have reportedly been sent to all alliance partners, including Congress, VCK, IUML, MDMK, CPI and CPM. Congress, VCK, IUML and MDMK have confirmed their attendance, while the Left parties are likely to stay away.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election. The initiative was planned as a symbolic gift to newborns and draws on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’.Under the scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around Rs 13,600.“Through this scheme, the government assumes the role of the maaman (uncle) for every child born in its institutions, presenting a gold ring as an enduring token of welcome,” a government order said.The scheme was originally scheduled to be launched on September 15, which coincides with the birth anniversary of former chief minister C N Annadurai.It will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday. The government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of the child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover all newborns delivered at government institutions. There will be no restriction based on birth order and no gender-based discrimination.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements. A project and programme management unit will also be established to oversee implementation and monitoring.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries each year, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or about 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are delivered at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents such as ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was intended to combine cultural significance with public healthcare.“Gold carries profound cultural and emotional resonance in Tamil Nadu. Gifting gold to a newborn celebrates the baby’s arrival, honours the mother’s noble journey and transforms public health delivery into a source of immense community pride,” the order said.
Article Summary: Under vijay's gold ring scheme, every newborn delivered at a government health facility will receive a one-gram gold ring. At the current gold rate, the ring is worth around rs 13,600. Vijay is set to meet european industrialists during the visit and pitch tamil nadu as an investment destination.
